title: GIST resection evidence by anatomical site
question: How do studies of esophageal and junctional GIST differ in how they report resection and patient selection?
scope: Compare an esophageal GIST case series with a junctional GIST matched report, focusing on procedure counts, patient selection and source limits.
reading_rule: Keep the clinical sites and analytic groups separate. Match the study's procedure and denominator to its original table before comparing results.

studies.task: Reported management pathways and endoscopic techniques in esophageal GIST
studies.title: Optimal Management Options for Esophageal Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors (E-GIST)

study_profile.study_design: Retrospective single-center descriptive case series with clinician-selected management
study_profile.evidence_type: Observational treatment-pattern, adverse-event and follow-up evidence
study_profile.population: Patients with pathologically confirmed esophageal GIST treated at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University
study_profile.primary_endpoint: Description of treatment allocation and postoperative clinical observations; no prespecified comparative primary endpoint is stated
study_profile.secondary_endpoint: Tumor characteristics, reported postoperative adverse events, follow-up and individual recurrence/death observations

cohorts.name: Single-center esophageal GIST series
cohorts.role: One retrospective descriptive cohort; the treatment groups are subsets of these same patients

selected_questions.question: How were treatment approaches distributed?
selected_questions.answer: There were 15 endoscopic resections, five direct operations, two operations after neoadjuvant imatinib, and one conservatively managed patient. The surgical total of seven already includes the two neoadjuvant-treated patients.

supporting_evidence.claim: Treatment allocation comprised 15 endoscopic resections, five direct operations, two operations after neoadjuvant imatinib, and one conservatively managed patient.
supporting_evidence.context: These four groups partition the same 23-patient series. The seven surgical patients in Table 3 include the five direct operations and two after neoadjuvant treatment; they are not an additional cohort. Treatment was selected by clinicians using tumor characteristics, not randomized.
supporting_evidence.source_locator: Publisher-layout PDF p. 2, Methods 2.3; pp. 3–4, Results 3.2; p. 4, Table 2 and Table 3 headings.

selected_questions.question: What endoscopic procedures and lesion sizes were reported?
selected_questions.answer: The 15 endoscopic procedures included nine STER, four ESD and two EMBL. Twelve tumors in this group were reported as no larger than 30 mm. This selected experience does not validate a universal treatment cutoff.

supporting_evidence.claim: Endoscopic management used three techniques, and 12 of the 15 endoscopically treated tumors were reported as no larger than 30 mm.
supporting_evidence.context: The series documents selected procedures and lesion sizes. It does not establish a universal treatment-size threshold or comparative oncologic equivalence to surgery.
supporting_evidence.source_locator: Publisher-layout PDF p. 4, Table 2; Results 3.3 and Table 3; p. 5, Discussion on selection and procedural limitations.

supports: The reported 23-patient case series and its mutually exclusive treatment allocations.
The three endoscopic techniques, lesion-size distribution, reported endoscopic events and specific follow-up observations.
Discussion of how clinician-selected case mix limits comparisons between endoscopic and surgical approaches.
does_not_establish: Superior safety, survival or oncologic equivalence of endoscopy versus surgery.
A validated universal size cutoff, treatment algorithm or replacement for clinical guidelines.
A causal effect of imatinib or any procedure on recurrence or survival.
Prospective, multicenter or externally validated outcomes.
A reconciled 2023 enrollment cutoff or corrected mitotic-index category.

limitations: The study is retrospective and includes 23 patients at one center. Treatment was chosen by experienced clinicians on the basis of tumor size, location, origin and growth pattern, creating strong selection differences between treatment groups.

No randomized comparison, adjusted treatment-effect estimate or external validation establishes superiority or oncologic equivalence. The discussion’s procedural suggestions are not independently validated selection rules.
The abstract and Methods 2.1 specify January 2017 to August 2023, whereas Results 3.1 says January 2017 to December 2023. No exact corrected end date is adopted.
Results 3.2 describes the highest mitotic-index category as >5/50 HPF, while Table 2 labels it >10/50 HPF. This category is excluded from the quantitative findings rather than silently corrected.

The manuscript discusses an earlier procedure and suspected recurrence in patient No. 21 without the original postoperative pathology. It is not used to derive an additional event rate, survival curve or effect estimate.

Postoperative adverse-event counts and follow-up are reported observations in small selected groups. No unreported confidence interval, standardized quality-of-life score or recurrence-rate estimate is generated.

The complete six-page publisher-layout PDF was reviewed. It contains no identified supplementary-results appendix or supplementary-file citation needed for the findings reproduced here; this does not assert that no supplementary resource exists elsewhere.

research_use.question: How do studies of esophageal and junctional GIST differ in how they report resection and patient selection?
research_use.question_zh: 食管与胃食管交界部GIST研究所报告的切除术式和患者选择有何不同？
research_use.answer: The esophageal series reports treatment allocation in 23 patients. Fifteen underwent endoscopic resection, seven had surgery, including two after neoadjuvant imatinib, and one was managed conservatively. The 15 endoscopic procedures included nine STER, four ESD and two EMBL. Twelve tumors in that subgroup measured no more than 30 mm. The junctional study focused on lesions measuring 2–5 cm and retrospectively compared endoscopic and laparoscopic resection using propensity matching. The abstract and Results disagree on unmatched allocation, and Table 1 labels the matched laparoscopic group n=20 while listing 10 men and 20 women. The studies describe different patient selection and procedure reporting. Their reported results leave comparative effectiveness and a general size cutoff unestablished.
research_use.answer_zh: 食管病例系列报告23名患者的治疗分配。15名接受内镜切除，7名接受手术（其中2名先接受新辅助伊马替尼），1名接受保守管理。15例内镜操作包括9例STER、4例ESD和2例EMBL，其中12个肿瘤不超过30毫米。胃食管交界部研究以2–5厘米病灶为主要纳入范围，用倾向评分匹配回顾性比较内镜和腹腔镜切除。摘要与结果中的未匹配组人数不一致，表1的匹配后腹腔镜组标注20人，但性别行列出10名男性和20名女性。两项研究描述了不同的患者选择和术式，现有结果尚不足以确认比较疗效或普适病灶尺寸阈值。
